# Reviewed question explanations

## What family size do the 2023 birth rates of the United States imply?

year-wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN-usa · births per woman · Reference answer: 1.6165

**How to estimate it:** Compare common family sizes and the share of people who never have children. Think about how birth timing can shift the rate in a given year.

1. Use the 2023 observation for the United States in “Fertility rate, total (births per woman)”.
2. The published value is 1.6165 births per woman.

**Reference assumptions:** The answer uses the frozen World Development Indicators observation. Definitions and reporting coverage can vary among countries.

- [World Bank · World Development Indicators](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SP.DYN.TFRT.IN): Fertility rate, total (births per woman). the United States, 2023: 1.6165 births per woman. Underlying source: World Population Prospects, United Nations (UN), publisher: UN Population Division;
Statistical databases and publications from national statistical offices, National Statistical Offices (NSOs);
Demographic Statistics, Eurostat (ESTAT).

## How many meatballs, plant balls and veggie balls did IKEA sell in its US restaurants in fiscal 2025?

world-ikea-balls · balls · Reference answer: 39923944

**How to estimate it:** Estimate annual store visits, the fraction who eat a ball-based meal, and balls per plate. Do not count every visitor as a diner.

1. For example: 60 million store visits × 8% ordering a ball meal × 8 balls ≈ 38.4 million balls. The dining share and serving size are illustrative.
2. Published reference: 39,923,944 balls.
3. A restaurant inside a furniture store can operate at the scale of a large food business.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses the cited publication’s figure at its stated precision and scope. The worked example uses illustrative assumptions; it does not define or prove the published total.

- [IKEA US · Annual Summary FY25, p.38](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/files/pdf/41/77/4177d8c1/us_annual_summary_fy25.pdf): 39,923,944 balls. US restaurants only; all three types combined. September 2024–August 2025.

## How many times does the International Space Station circle Earth in 24 hours?

world-iss-day · orbits · Reference answer: 16

**How to estimate it:** Estimate the distance around Earth and the station’s speed. Divide to get an orbit time, then compare with a full day.

1. For scale: roughly 40,000 km around Earth ÷ roughly 28,000 km/hour ≈ 1.4 hours per circuit; allowing for altitude gives roughly 16 circuits per day.
2. Published reference: 16 orbits.
3. An astronaut’s orbital day is much shorter than the day on the ground.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses the cited publication’s figure at its stated precision and scope. The worked example uses illustrative assumptions; it does not define or prove the published total.

- [NASA · ISS facts and figures](https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/space-station-facts-and-figures/): 16 orbits. Use NASA’s rounded orbital rate, not Earth’s daily rotation.

## How far apart are New York (JFK) and Beijing (PEK) airports?

year-route-great-circle-jfk-pek · kilometres · Reference answer: 10978.539502975163

**How to estimate it:** Picture the two airports on a map. A degree of latitude is about 111 km, but east–west degrees get shorter toward the poles. Compare with a familiar distance on the same continent.

1. Use the airports’ published coordinates and the great-circle distance on a spherical Earth.
2. With a mean radius of 6,371 km, the shortest surface distance is approximately 10,978.54 km.

**Reference assumptions:** This is a geographic distance between airport coordinates. Real flight paths can be longer because of airspace, weather and routing.

- [OurAirports · airport coordinates](https://ourairports.com/data/): JFK latitude/longitude: 40.639447, -73.779317. PEK latitude/longitude: 40.077349, 116.596702.

## How many pairs of Adidas shoes were made in Vietnam in 2023?

world-vietnam-adidas · pairs · Reference answer: 118180000

**How to estimate it:** Estimate worldwide demand for the brand, then the share supplied by Vietnam. Think about athletic-shoe buyers and how much manufacturing is concentrated in a few countries.

1. One rough route: 2 billion buyers × 1 pair/year × 15% brand share × one-third made in Vietnam ≈ 100 million pairs. The report instead gives 311 million pairs globally and a 38% Vietnam share.
2. Published reference: 118.18 million pairs (311 × 38%). In the answer unit: 118.18 × 1000000 ≈ 118,180,000 pairs.
3. The published country share is rounded, so the reference is an approximate allocation of output, not an exact factory count.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses an allocation calculated from the report’s rounded total and country share. It is approximate, not an exact unit-by-unit count.

- [Adidas · Annual Report 2023, sourcing](https://report.adidas-group.com/2023/en/group-management-report-our-company/global-operations.html): 118.18 million pairs (311 × 38%). Adidas footwear only; pairs, not individual shoes.

**How to estimate it:** Estimate the exposed surface area of the metalwork, coverage per litre and paint mass per litre. Both sides of many beams need coating.

2. Published reference: 60 tonnes of paint.
3. An open lattice has much more paintable surface than its silhouette suggests.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses the cited publication’s figure at its stated precision and scope. The worked example uses illustrative assumptions; it does not define or prove the published total.

- [Eiffel Tower · painting the tower](https://www.toureiffel.paris/en/the-monument/painting-eiffel-tower): 60 tonnes of paint. Use the operator’s standard repainting-campaign estimate; paint applied, not accumulated old paint.

## How many fans did the Boston Red Sox draw per home game in 2008?

year-baseball-attendance-bos-2008 · spectators per home game · Reference answer: 37632.71604938272

**How to estimate it:** Estimate the ballpark’s capacity and how full it is on weeknights versus weekends. Include the less popular games when averaging.

1. The regular-season record reports attendance = 3,048,250, Ghome = 81.

## How many lightning flashes occur worldwide in an average second?

world-lightning · flashes per second · Reference answer: 40

**How to estimate it:** Estimate how many thunderstorms are active at once and flashes per minute in an average storm. Most storms are not directly above you.

1. For example: 2,000 active storms × 1 flash/minute ÷ 60 ≈ 33 flashes/second. Storm intensity varies widely; this is a rough model.
2. Published reference: 40 flashes per second.
3. Flashes inside clouds count too, so ground-strike maps do not show the entire total.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses the cited study’s published estimate, not an exact census. Research uncertainty is real; the worked example is only a way to estimate its scale.

- [NOAA · JetStream lightning](https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/lightning): 40 flashes per second. Include cloud-to-cloud and cloud-to-ground flashes. Use NOAA’s rounded satellite-based estimate.

## If a belt around Earth were lifted one metre off the ground everywhere, how much longer would it need to be?

fermi-earth-belt · metres · Reference answer: 6.283185307179586

**How to estimate it:** Compare the old and new circumferences algebraically. Both include the same Earth-radius term, which cancels out.

1. Original circumference = 2πR.
2. Raised circumference = 2π(R + 1).
3. Extra length = 2π ≈ 6.283 metres, regardless of Earth’s size.

**Reference assumptions:** A circular belt raised one metre radially everywhere above a spherical Earth. The result depends only on the lift height, not the size of Earth.

- [OpenStax · circular motion](https://openstax.org/books/college-physics/pages/6-1-rotation-angle-and-angular-velocity): The circumference relation C = 2πr.

## How fast does Earth travel around the Sun?

fermi-orbit-speed-earth · kilometres per second · Reference answer: 29.78975630914016

**How to estimate it:** Picture a circular orbit. Estimate its radius in Earth–Sun distances, find its circumference, and divide by the planet’s orbital period.

1. Orbit length ≈ 2π × 149,600,000 = 939,965,000 km.
2. 365.2 days × 86,400 = 31,553,300 seconds.
3. Distance ÷ time ≈ 29.7898 km/s.

**Reference assumptions:** A circular-orbit estimate using the mean orbital radius and period. Real speed changes around an elliptical orbit.

## At its farthest orbital alignment, how long would a radio signal take to go from Earth to Mars and back?

fermi-radio-mars-farthest · minutes · Reference answer: 41.955555555555556

**How to estimate it:** At the nearest alignment, subtract orbital radii; at the farthest alignment, add them. Double the separation for a reply, then divide by light speed.

1. One-way separation ≈ sum of the orbital radii = 377,600,000 km.
2. Round-trip distance ≈ 755,200,000 km.
3. At 300,000 km/s, that is ≈ 41.9556 minutes.

**Reference assumptions:** Circular, coplanar reference orbits and an immediate reply. Actual orbital eccentricity, signal routing and processing delays are excluded.

- [NASA · planetary fact sheets](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/): Mean orbital distances from the Sun.

**Reference assumptions:** Use a 24-hour rotation and the 6,371 km mean Earth radius. Count motion around Earth’s axis only; orbital motion is excluded.

## How many hours of Netflix did people watch worldwide during 2023?

world-netflix · hours · Reference answer: 183000000000

**How to estimate it:** Estimate subscribing households, average daily viewing time per household, and days in the year. Account for households that rarely watch.

1. For example: 250 million households × 2 hours/day × 365 ≈ 182.5 billion hours. This is a household viewing model, not an assertion about the average individual.
2. Published reference: 183 billion hours. In the answer unit: 183 × 1000000000 ≈ 183,000,000,000 hours.

## How many Earth volumes would fit inside Jupiter?

nasa-jupiter-volume · Earth volumes · Reference answer: 1321.3319670239382

**How to estimate it:** Volume grows with the cube of a length scale. An elevenfold diameter suggests roughly eleven cubed, or about thirteen hundred Earth volumes.

1. An elevenfold size ratio gives 11 × 11 × 11 = 1,331 as a quick estimate.
2. NASA lists Jupiter’s volume as 143,128 and Earth’s as 108.321, both in units of 10¹⁰ km³.
3. Volume ratio ≈ 143,128 ÷ 108.321 ≈ 1,321.33 Earth volumes.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses NASA’s published planetary volumes. Cubing equatorial diameters would overestimate the ratio because Jupiter is flattened at the poles. This is volume equivalence, not sphere packing.

- [NASA · Jupiter fact sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html): Jupiter volume 143,128 and Earth volume 108.321 in units of 10¹⁰ km³.

## If the oceans were spread evenly over a smooth Earth, how deep would the water be?

fermi-ocean-global-layer · kilometres · Reference answer: 2.623197798878733

**How to estimate it:** Estimate the total volume of ocean water. Divide by the area of the smooth sphere it would cover.

1. Surface area ≈ 4π × 6,371² = 510,064,000 km².
2. Ocean volume ≈ 1.338 billion km³.
3. Uniform depth ≈ volume ÷ area = 2.6232 km.

**Reference assumptions:** The reference smooths away all land and seabed relief and divides ocean volume by the entire Earth’s surface area.

## How fast was Parker Solar Probe moving near its December 2024 closest approach to the Sun?

world-parker-closest-pass · kilometres per second · Reference answer: 192.2272

**How to estimate it:** Compare Earth’s orbital speed with a probe travelling much closer to the Sun. The characteristic orbital speed grows with the inverse square root of distance, and a fast flyby can be faster still.

1. If a spacecraft passes at one twentieth of Earth’s orbital distance, the local circular speed is about 4.5 times Earth’s 30 km/s. An eccentric orbit can raise the speed further.
2. Published reference: 430,000 miles per hour. In the answer unit: 430,000 × 0.00044704000000000006 ≈ 192.2272 kilometres per second.
3. The record speed refers to the brief close approach, while the spacecraft moves more slowly farther from the Sun.

**Reference assumptions:** The score uses the cited publication’s figure at its stated precision and scope. The worked example uses illustrative assumptions; it does not define or prove the published total.

- [NASA · Parker Solar Probe closest pass](https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/heliophysics/nasas-parker-solar-probe-makes-history-with-closest-pass-to-sun/): 430,000 miles per hour. Use NASA’s rounded speed relative to the Sun for the December 2024 pass.
